brief: GS reads a squeeze setup: its Monetary Policy Factor sits at -8, near the bottom of its 30-year range, hedge fund US net positioning is at the 0th percentile, and clients have moved into protection mode into year-end. Non-dealers sold $63.7bn of S&P futures over six weeks, over 70% from long liquidation rather than new shorts, while asset-manager longs track inversely with 10-year real yields; a 25bp real-yield jump drove $5.5bn more liquidation, so GS argues a yield rollover would reverse the de-risking. Russell 2000 positioning is similarly washed out (7th percentile, record leveraged shorts), with some short covering already underway. Macro traders have also shifted into fixed-income ETF options (HYG, LQD, TLT, IEF) as SPX stops reacting to macro news. BofA says 5% Treasury yields now compete with equities for capital, and lays out a 5/6/7 framework where returns worsen progressively above 6% and 7%; it places the market in the mildest, first bucket. MOVE has jumped from 77 to 113. DB argues the "Fed put" is less reliable now because inflation, unlike the 2010s, remains above target. TS Lombard expects France's OAT-Bund spread to widen past 200bp before the ECB intervenes, as Japanese investors repatriate OAT holdings.
